newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan ends ceiling on consigned oil product sales.
newsitem.headline: Japan ends ceiling on consigned oil product sales.

text.p: Japan's Ministry of International Trade and Industry (MITI) said on Tuesday it had lifted a restriction on the domestic sale of oil products refined by domestic refiners under consignment from overseas companies.

Previously Japanese companies could not sell in the domestic market more than 50 percent of oil products they refined under consignment arrangements with overseas firms. That ceiling was lifted on January 3.
"(Japanese companies) are now free to sell on the domestic market as much as they want of the oil products they refine under consignment," a trade ministry official said.
A foreign company will sometimes not need all of the products from oil refined for it on a consignment basis and will sell those products to the refining firm.

MITI's latest move was part of a sweeping industry deregulation that began last year. In April Japan liberalised its oil products import market, allowing companies other than oil firms to import oil products such as gasoline and kerosene.
China, South Korea, Taiwan and Singapore are some of the major countries that consign oil for processing in Japan, the MITI official said.
The MITI official said Japanese refineries' crude oil throughput is roughly five million barrels-per-day (bpd) and that consigned processing accounted for about five to six percent of that.
